summary: This article explains how builders in the Najd region of Saudi Arabia have long used sun-dried mud brick to build homes that stay cool in the heat, and how they decorate the walls with carved triangle patterns.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Mud-Brick Architecture of Najd”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: made to look attractive rather than only useful
a skilled worker who makes things carefully by hand
a careful way of doing something that takes skill

challengeTerms.def: made of shapes like lines, triangles, and circles arranged in a regular design
able to continue for a long time without running out or causing harm

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that old building methods like mud brick still have something useful to teach us today? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how mud brick helps a home stay comfortable in the hot, dry climate of Najd.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review decorative, craftsman, and technique, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use geometric, thermal, and sustainable in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
